exposure: Indications for cesarean section (e.g., previous scar, fetal distress, prolonged labor)
cohort: Mothers who delivered in Bowen University Teaching Hospital, Nigeria, between June 1, 2018, and May 31, 2022.
finding: The study found a cesarean section prevalence of 38.2% at Bowen University Teaching Hospital, which is higher than the WHO-recommended rate, with previous scar as the leading indication and anemia as the most common adverse outcome among those who had a CS.
mod_finding: The prevalence of cesarean section deliveries was 38.2%, exceeding WHO recommendations, and 15.6% of women who underwent a cesarean section experienced adverse outcomes, predominantly anemia.
